reachable: Yes, and it fires. Executed the real genome's batcher + stream + collate on the local encoded pack (data/dockerfs3-cupsF-treat-nocwd, split_train_dev seed 0, bs=64, n≈1890 command rows per batch). (a) Trajectory recovery is exact: _trajectory_ids(prev) equals the true per-sequence segment id on every batch tested (6 batches spanning steps 1..4000) — prev_full = cat([zeros, tgt[:,:-1]]) is exactly zero only at step 0 of each sequence, and collate pads at the end so masked rows are contiguous and in step order. (b) The miner flags 123-159 rows per batch (~8% of rows), all of them (cat, cat) pairs — mv/redirect empty observations are excluded by the rarity cap exactly as claimed. (c) The WRI term is live and gets gradient: with the real net trained 6 steps through evolve/harness._train, the harness detected WANTS_CTX, passed ctx on every call, and full-loss minus parent-equivalent loss averaged +2.26 per step. Gradient flows only to pred[rows] — 123/1893 rows receive WRI gradient, ||g_wri||/||g_full|| ≈ 0.23 with a near-oracle predictor. (d) The specific hard negative the hypothesis names is present: for all 310 cups renamed-read rows across 6 batches, the exposure row of the name-matched decoy (`cat <path>` for a read of `cat <path>.N`) is in the kept candidate set — 310/310. (e) Not degenerate positionally: the positive's rank among kept candidates spreads over 0-11+ and the step gap j-i over 2-11, so the term is not teaching a fixed offset. (f) With ctx=None or with no flagged rows, the loss is bit-identical to the parent r12_antiretrieval_ring_negatives (torch.equal True), as claimed. (g) The head does not bypass the arch: r3's wrap adds a residual `contrib` to pred rather than recomputing it, so r23's pointer injection survives — the crossover keeps both mechanisms as stated. Nothing runs at the scored position: the objective is invoked only from evolve/harness._train and eval/guard_reach.
solves_outside_model: No. The mining is loss-side only. It reads tgt (the training target), ctx["cmd"] and ctx["prev"], all under @torch.no_grad, and uses them to (i) select which rows get a term and (ii) label a cross-entropy — both explicitly permitted. Nothing is written into b["tok"], the objective never touches the batch dict, and it does not mutate its inputs in place (every assignment is on a freshly derived tensor). G.load_objective is referenced only at eval/adapter.py:115 (handed to H._train) and eval/guard_reach.py:176; evolve/cups_probe.py and evolve/cups_ca.py never call it, so at scoring time this code does not execute at all. The one thing that reaches "the future" is the batch-wide rarity count (dup.sum over all rows including later ones), which is a loss-side statistic of the same kind as the parent's in-batch negatives — the hypothesis states this explicitly. The WRI candidate set itself is restricted to strictly earlier rows of the same trajectory. The prior-retraction shape (resolving the move chain in Python and stamping the answer into the model's input) does not occur here; the stream is unmodified baseline_interleave and the model still has to integrate the mv commands.
summary: This is an unusually accurate hypothesis. Every mechanical claim I could execute checks out, including several the author could not have run (no torch in the jail) and correctly flagged as unmeasured. The base loss is the parent r12 objective verbatim and is bit-identical to it when the new term is inert. Trajectory-id recovery from the zero previous-observation works exactly. The miner fires on ~8% of rows, is 99.7% precise against raw observation text, and mines precisely the pairs the hypothesis names: cups expose→renamed-read (`cat .../app.ini` → `cat .../app.ini.1`, `cat .../f528.tmp` → `cat .../f528.tmp.8`) and cvar produce→test (`cat s0.dat` → `cat out.dat`); the flagged split is 310 cups / 550 cvar / 8 other. The hard negative the hypothesis is built around — the content originally exposed at the read's own path — is in the candidate set for 310 of 310 cups renamed-read rows. The WRI distance is `sum((a-b)^2)/D`, which is exactly the probe's decision variable `((c - pred_obs)**2).mean(-1)` at evolve/cups_probe.py:147, so the "same decision variable the retrieval arms use" claim is literal. Only three minor imprecisions: the candidate set is ~17 rows but only ~10 distinct contents (7 are the repeated blank mv observation); the "r3 carries an equivalent content-preservation term" reassurance is vacuous on this arch because r23 has no transition_from_emb (so both that term and the dropped r18 head are dead); and the rarity cap costs 23% recall on genuine content re-reads, which the author predicted as a risk and which I confirmed loses examples without corrupting labels. None of these change what the candidate is or what it will be archived as. What I could NOT check: (1) all measurements are on the local dockerfs3-cupsF-treat-nocwd pack — if scoring runs against a blend spec via TWM_TRAIN_ROOT, the mining rates on the composed set are unmeasured; (2) whether the term actually moves comp_ca — I ran 6 CPU steps, not the 4000-step budget, and never ran the probe; (3) GPU wall clock for r23 arch + r3 head + this loss combined (loss alone is 43ms vs the parent's 26ms on CPU at n≈1890, negligible against forward/backward, but the author's own "have not measured the combined wall clock" caveat stands); (4) whether the term could teach a move-order-position heuristic that scores positive on the frozen slice — the spread of positive rank and step gap in training argues against it, but that is evidence, not proof.

divergences.claim: "At each flagged row the prediction is trained with a cross-entropy ... an N-way forced choice among the contents that trajectory has already shown."
divergences.what_the_code_does: The candidate set is exactly what section 3 of the hypothesis specifies (earlier rows of the same trajectory, minus near-duplicates of the positive, plus the positive). But on real batches the mean candidate count is 16.7 while the mean number of DISTINCT observation texts among them is 10.0, because ~6.9 candidates per row are the identical empty mv/redirect observation ('cwd=... exit=0\n'). Those share one target vector, so they carry identical logits and collectively soak softmax mass rather than acting as distinct contents.

divergences.claim: "The partner's head (r18_transition_forwardmodel_consistency) is dropped: it returns 0.0 on any arch without that operator, and r3's aux already carries an equivalent content-preservation term on the same operator, guarded the same way."
divergences.what_the_code_does: Both halves are literally true, but on THIS genome the substitute is also dead: r23_dual_address_transport_pointer (and its base r22_prefix_content_xattention, and seq_worldmodel) define no transition_from_emb, so r3's trans_weight block at head/r3_rename_registry_occupancy_routing.py:382 never fires either. Nothing is lost by dropping r18, but no content-preservation supervision is retained by keeping r3 — a reader could take the sentence the other way.

divergences.claim: "If the rarity cap of 4 is too tight ... That loses examples but does not corrupt any." (stated as an unmeasured risk)
divergences.what_the_code_does: Measured and confirmed in the direction the author guessed, with a real cost: on genuine content re-reads (a `cat` row whose observation text exactly equals that of an earlier row of the same trajectory issued by a different command, output >= 20 chars) the miner's recall is 0.766, and 43 of the 45 misses are the rarity cap (duplicate counts 5-16). Precision is 0.997 (865/868 mined positives have byte-identical observation text; the 3 misses are near-identical `ls` listings).
